tytul: Rose petals in honey: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for rose petals kept in honey.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to Oregon State University Extension, covering food with honey does not preserve it: lab trials found bacteria growing where the food meets the honey.

Oregon State University Extension limits high-moisture, low-acid ingredients, such as fresh garlic or herbs, to no more than 15% of a honey infusion by weight, using hot infusion only, with the honey kept above 140°F (60°C).
Do not give honey or products made with honey to infants under 1 year of age.
The Polish National Centre for Nutrition Education (NCEŻ) lists honey among the foods an infant should avoid because of the risk of poisoning.

According to NDSU Extension, some flowers should not be eaten, so identify flowers correctly before eating them; flowers from a florist are meant to look at, not to eat, because some pesticides used on them have not been approved for edible plants.

akapity: Herbs, flowers and infusions made from them are not naturally acidic; to be canned, they need a tested recipe with an added amount of acid, sugar or both, even when the infusion is strained.
Honey ranges in pH from 3.1 to 6.1, and some pathogens can grow at a pH as low as 3.7; honey is kept safe by its low water activity, not by its acidity.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for rose petals in honey from a checked source.
